title: Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: [Berakhot 47b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.47b.7) relates that Rami bar Chama did not count Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa toward the zimmun, although, in Hyman’s wording, he had learned Sifra, Sifrei and Mekhilta. When Rami bar Chama died, Rava said that he died only because he had not counted Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa. The passage explains that Rav Menashya served the Rabbis; alternatively, he heard teachings directly from the Rabbis and repeated them. Hyman cites [Berakhot 49b](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.49b.2) and [Pesachim 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.6b.7) in support: they have him transmitting in Rav’s name. In Yoma 78 ([compare Yoma 78a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.78a.11)), Rav Menashya bar Tachlifa reports Rav Amram, who reports Rabbah bar bar Chana, etc.[^4]

notes.text: The issue is counting toward zimmun, not a dinner invitation. The checked text has Sifra, Sifrei and hilkheta, while Hyman supplies Mekhilta. His גרים is understood as repeating the teachings, supported by the checked וגריס להו.
The supplied Yoma reference is עח followed by a comma, then א״ר (“said Rabbi”), not an explicit side-a marker. It is rendered folio 78 without assigning a side.

The consulted Berakhot 47b has Sifra, Sifrei and hilkheta, whereas Hyman supplies Mekhilta. It concerns counting toward zimmun and preserves the two explanations concerning his relation to the Rabbis. The supplied Yoma folio 78 has no explicit side; no side is added here.

[Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2526&lang=en) gives “Sifra, Sifrei and halakhah,” like the consulted Berakhot; Hyman gives Mekhilta as the third work. Yoma 78a records the full transmission from Menashya to Rav Amram to Rabbah bar bar Chana.
